Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Greenline: request for Private deployment architecture dossier and evidence

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our InfoSec team is pulling together the SIG/CAIQ and SOC 2 evidence pack for our procurement board. They asked for a concise "security architectural dossier" describing how Redwood's Private deployment isolates tenant workloads from the control plane and other tenants, plus an inventory of diagrams/evidence we can attach.

Specifically they'd like:
- A single-page logical diagram showing VPCs, control-plane endpoints, and permitted egress paths for Private deployments.
- A short narrative (200-400 words) explaining the tenant isolation model and fallback behavior when a Dedicated pool is unavailable.
- A CSV or table mapping SIG/CAIQ network controls to your artifacts (diagram filenames, logs, playbooks).

Can you share a packaged bundle and a short summary we can include in the CAIQ response? We need this by COB Wednesday (2026-08-12) if possible.

Appreciate it — Claudia
Security Programs, Greenline

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Greenline: request for Private deployment architecture dossier and evidence

Claudia —

Thanks for the clear list. Kimberley and I pulled together an initial package and a short narrative below. The attachments referenced here are the files we included in the Drive link (shared above). If you need anything redacted for your procurement packet, tell us which fields and we’ll provide a redacted copy.

Summary (short):
Redwood Private deployments separate tenant compute from Redwood control-plane and shared services via a two-tier isolation model: 1) Network segmentation by customer VPCs with strict egress ACLs that only permit outbound traffic to explicitly whitelisted service endpoints (e.g., KMS, telemetry ingestion), and 2) Control-plane authentication and per-tenant credential scoping so that control-plane operations (deploys, model routing) are authorized only with tenant-specific keys and claims. We support an air-gapped option (no outbound internet) and a VPC-peering/Transit option for customers who require managed connectivity.

Key points included in attachments:
- private-stack-network-diagram-v3.png: logical layers (tenant VPCs, management/control subnet, egress proxy, KMS boundary).
- segmentation-evidence.csv: mapping of SIG/CAIQ network controls to artifacts (diagrams, config exports, firewall rules).
- control-plane-matrix.pdf: control-plane trust domains and key provisioning flow.

Operational fallback: when Dedicated capacity is unavailable we route inference traffic to the nearest compatible Private pool within the customer’s region while honoring data residency and encryption policies. If the customer requested an air-gapped deployment, we do not route externally; instead we failover to reserved on-prem capacity or queued requests per the customer SLA.

ETA: attaching the three files and a Drive bundle now.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Greenline: request for Private deployment architecture dossier and evidence

Claudia,

Adding a few clarifying bullets for the SIG/CAIQ mapping and SOC 2 narrative sections:

- Network segmentation: tenant VPCs are logically isolated; Control-plane endpoints live in a separate management VPC with IAM-scoped service accounts. We provide exported VPC flow logs and a sample egress ACL that demonstrates default-deny with per-service allow rules (see segmentation-evidence.csv).

- Key management: customer-managed KMS (optional) or Redwood-managed KMS with per-tenant key envelopes. KMS audit logs can be delivered on request; see control-plane-matrix.pdf for the key provisioning flow.

- Telemetry and logs: telemetry is encrypted in transit via TLS and stored in a restricted logs bucket; access is role-based and auditable. We included an excerpt of our log retention policy in the Drive bundle.

- Air-gapped option: for fully air-gapped deployments we ship a package that includes an on-site control plane mirror and local KV store; this configuration requires a separate compliance review and statement of work.

If you want a condensed one-page narrative for the CAIQ narrative field (Q# network-1 style), say the word and I’ll draft it today.

—Kim
Head of Security Architecture — Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Claudia
